For guidance only: sets the method, tax year and summary of the tax worksheet. Rows always show neutral facts.

Moving average per coin and wallet – not across wallets (KryptowährungsVO § 2). Rewards enter new holdings at acquisition cost 0 (BMF: staking / airdrops) – the income file lists them at value on receipt. Fees are not deductible for holdings acquired from 1 Mar 2021 (§ 27a(4) no. 2, § 20(2) EStG): cost and proceeds without fees. Lending interest (type from the CSV import or note) is income on receipt at 27.5 percent and keeps that value as acquisition cost.

Staking with coins you already hold and airdrops: the value on receipt does not matter for tax – by law the acquisition cost is 0 (§ 27b Abs. 2 EStG; BMF “Kryptowährungen”). Tax only applies when you sell.

Sales and fees paid in crypto are disposals – swaps are deferred. A crypto fee on a sale counts in the price before fees – otherwise it is its own disposal at its value. Portfolio value from daily closes – a missing close leaves the cost empty.

A network fee paid in crypto (transfer to your own wallet, withdrawal) is a disposal of the fee coins at market value – gain or loss only on those coins, not a loss of the whole fee (%1$s). Without a recorded price: previous day’s close; without a close the proceeds stay empty.
Specific identification is not supported – FIFO is used.
A gift marked “to spouse / civil partner” is no gain and no loss: proceeds = your cost basis, which your partner takes over (%1$s).

Selling crypto for a stablecoin (USDT/USDC/DAI …) that you keep is crypto-to-crypto here and not taxed – record it as a swap into the stablecoin. Only a sale for euros is taxed – “Sell” counts as a sale for euros.
The same applies to a USDT or cash fee on a transfer between your own wallets: it is not added to the cost basis and is listed as information only.
Matching per HMRC: same day → next 30 days → Section 104 pool.

Transition 1 Jan 2025 (Rev. Proc. 2024-28 safe harbor): if earlier years used FIFO across all wallets, the remaining lots as of 31 Dec 2024 go to the wallets holding the coins – the wallet with the oldest coins gets the oldest cost basis.
From tax year 2025 the IRS requires cost basis per wallet or exchange (Rev. Proc. 2024-28): the export uses FIFO per wallet from 2025 and your cost method for earlier years.
A withdrawal fee in USDT or cash is not a loss: a cash fee is not a deductible cost, a USDT fee is a disposal at par without gain – it is listed as information only (%1$s).
